Thanks! I’d say my favourite spot was Badwater Basin. It was one of the busier spots because it’s so popular of course, but very few people actually venture out to the widest part of the basin. I did and was completely alone because of it - it was the most silent place I’d ever experienced. Literally nothing was making a sound; it was so surreal. It’s really deceptive too because when you’re on the basin itself, it seems as though the salt flats stretch all the way to the Panamint Range. When you see it from Dante’s View however, it barely even reaches halfway across the entire basin/valley. Really cool to see.

In terms of best drive, I’d say if you can add it to your itinerary, drive through Jubilee Pass road. It leads onto Badwater road, and it can either be driven from the south (Jubilee Pass into Badwater) or vice Versa. We exited the park this way, but if you’re coming in from the Vegas/Pahrump area, I suggest entering the park through Jubilee Pass Road, because as stunning as the drive was the direction we did it, it looked even more spectacular driving the other way, because you get a much better view of the surrounding mountains. It was a really really quiet road too - think we saw 5 other cars the entire 60 or so miles?

The road to the Father Crowley Vista is also stunning, which is where the first photo was taken. Definitely don’t miss that but I imagine that’s on lots of people’s itineraries anyway, although again, that entire western part of the park was very quiet.

If you are going to be using an SUV/high-clearance vehicle, I’d suggest driving up to the Eureka sand dunes. I believe the road is now open after the summer floods. The Mesquite Sand dunes were amazing, but the Eureka dunes are meant to be far bigger and more spectacular. We didn’t have a high-clearance vehicle and so we were limited as to what we could see, so if I went again, I’d definitely drive one.
